drug_class: Nerve growth factor / corneal healing eye drop
purpose: This eye drop is used to treat a serious eye condition called neurotrophic keratitis, which is when the nerves in your cornea (the clear front part of your eye) stop working properly. This can cause your cornea to break down and form sores or ulcers. The medicine helps heal those sores and restore your eye's health.
how_it_works: Your cornea normally relies on tiny nerves to stay healthy and repair itself. In neurotrophic keratitis, those nerves are damaged and your cornea struggles to heal on its own. Cenegermin-bkbj is a man-made version of a natural protein called nerve growth factor, and it works by signaling your cornea cells to grow, repair, and protect themselves again.
common_side_effects: Eye pain or discomfort, eye redness, tearing or watery eyes, eye discharge, and mild blurring of vision. Some people also notice a foreign body sensation, like something is in their eye.
warnings: Do not use while wearing contact lenses — remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting. This medicine must be stored in the freezer and thawed before use, following specific handling instructions. Tell your doctor about all other eye drops you use, and wait at least 15 minutes between using different eye medications. If you notice sudden vision changes or worsening eye pain, contact your eye doctor right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop in the affected eye 6 times a day, every 2 hours during waking hours, for 8 weeks. Your eye doctor will guide you on the exact schedule. It helps to set reminders so you do not miss doses.
